title: A Little Waxy Refresh
content:
If you read Waxy.org entirely via RSS, you may not have noticed that I’ve refreshed the site a bit. Or even if you visit it, you may not have noticed!

I’ve made a bunch of small incremental changes over the last few weeks. Nothing major, mostly fixing a lot of long-standing issues and polishing rough edges that have bothered me for years.

The most notable changes are the redesigned archives and search features, which try to better surface some of my last 24 years of writing here. It includes starred long-form posts, highlighting some of my favorites over the years.

I added better credits to the linkblog, showing a site name, domain, or social media username instead of just the bare “via” link, and added that into the RSS feed for better attribution.

I cleaned up the comments design, which was frankly kind of ugly. It now does a better job of remembering who you are if you’re posting on the same device, but without requiring auth.

I also refreshed the About page, updating my bio, past, and current projects. The header and footer finally includes links to Waxy’s automated accounts on Bluesky and Mastodon, the only two social media apps I still feel comfortable using, and a new icon for RSS, which everyone should use but hardly anyone does. I refreshed the type across the site, and there’s a proper 404 page now.

Finally, I added a tiny easter egg in the logo for desktop users.

Tiny changes, but they all add up to something I’m pretty happy with.

The first half of this year was pretty rough for me and my wife, dealing with the fallout from the deaths of my uncle and her father, spending months apart, caring for others and picking up the pieces. (The worst seems to be behind us now.)

Since then, I’ve found some comfort in spending time getting my digital life in order: migrating my outdated servers, verifying backups, getting everything safely checked into source control, and brushing off the cobwebs.

These small changes to Waxy were the first in a series of updates to long-dormant projects of mine: some small, some pretty big. I’ll post more on that over the next few days.
author: Andy Baio
